If Donald Trump and his cronies spent as much energy actually listening to
Americans and doing what voters want as they have on their freakout about the
[spotlight on Natalie Harp](https://zeteo.com/p/who-is-natalie-harp-the-trump-
aide), perhaps the president's approval rating wouldn't have [dipped to
33%](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-approval-falls-33-lowest-his-
presidency-reutersipsos-poll-finds-2026-08-17/) this week.

While Trump's allies rushed to the
[defense](https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/2026/08/ossoff-trump-natalie-
harp/688365/) of Harp, the president's close and influential aide dubbed the
"[human printer](https://www.ft.com/content/0eb4e7ce-42e3-49af-
ae27-645eb7676fad?syn-25a6b1a6=1)," his administration was busy further
harming democracy, undermining the Constitution, and hurting societies
worldwide.

This week, Trump's newly sworn-in attorney general, Todd Blanche,
[refused](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ovwCBL3NVWE) to pledge that his
Justice Department would act independently of the White House. That's
troubling but not surprising when it comes to Trump's cronies, given we also
learned this week the DOJ [sought to
interview](https://apnews.com/article/justice-department-trump-
maralago-b561cf695c2b8476a4320b03155c3d90) FBI agents involved in the 2022
classified documents search of Mar-a-Lago. And Trump's DOJ is [preparing to
deploy](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/us-law-week/doj-plans-to-
deploy-1-000-monitors-to-watch-midterm-elections) about 1,000 "election
monitors" for the midterms.

Here's more from 'This Week in Democracy - Week 83':

#### **Saturday, Aug. 15 - Trump DOJ's 'Ridiculous Fishing Expedition' Into
Law Firm**

The _New York Times_
[reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/15/us/politics/prosecutors-
examined-firm-with-tie-to-judge-in-trump-hush-money-trial.html) that, over the
past year, Chicago prosecutors have investigated a Democratic fundraising firm
that was previously co-owned by the daughter of the judge who oversaw Trump's
2024 hush money trial, which ended in his conviction on 34 felony counts.

The founder of the firm, Mike Nellis, called the move "a ridiculous fishing
expedition based on conspiracy theories that are completely divorced from
reality," and accused Trump's DOJ of trying to seize "sensitive political
communications of my clients," including Joe Biden and Kamala Harris.

#### **Sunday, Aug. 16 - Blanche Won't Pledge Independence**

During an interview on 'Meet the Press,' former Trump defense lawyer and
newly-minted Attorney General Todd Blanche
[suggested](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/attorney-
general-todd-blanche-doj-state-voter-rolls-supreme-court-rcna592721) the
Justice Department may ask the Supreme Court to overturn the nearly two dozen
lawsuits the DOJ has lost trying to force states to turn over their voter
rolls.

He also [refused](https://x.com/bulwarkonline/status/2088990893214761141?s=46)
to pledge that the DOJ would act independently of the White House, saying, "No
attorney general should ever pledge that."

#### **Monday, Aug. 17 - Trump's DOJ to Deploy 1,000 Election Monitors for
Midterms**

Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon told Bloomberg that Trump's Justice
Department is [planning](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/us-law-week/doj-plans-
to-deploy-1-000-monitors-to-watch-midterm-elections) to deploy about 1,000
monitors during the midterm elections in November.

It's unclear where the monitors will be assigned, but she hinted that they may
be sent to jurisdictions where the DOJ alleges there may be "voter fraud
issues," despite the fact that voter fraud is [nearly non-
existent](https://www.brennancenter.org/topics/voting-elections/vote-
suppression/myth-voter-fraud).

#### **Tuesday, Aug. 18 - Trump's Antisemitism Probes Against Universities
'Predetermined'**

Multiple outlets [reported](https://apnews.com/article/trump-harvard-justice-
department-brown-columbia-3e2519fac8b1d85caa74b7ff1ff63744) that a Monday
whistleblower disclosure
[revealed](https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28562760-title-vi-
whistleblower-disclosure-for-congress) that the outcomes of the Trump
administration's investigations into three Ivy League universities over
allegations of antisemitism constituted an "unlawful process designed to
achieve predetermined political goals" that were "without regard for the
evidence."

Meanwhile, Secretary of State Marco Rubio
[announced](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cnvnl0elz47o) sanctions against
the International Criminal Court president who issued an arrest warrant for
Russian President Vladimir Putin's arrest, along with one of the Court's
senior lawyers.

#### **Wednesday, Aug. 19 - Trump's 'Laughable' Voter Report**

NPR [reported](https://www.npr.org/2026/08/19/nx-s1-5938799/trump-census-
bureau-noncitizen-voting) that the Census Bureau report Trump
[cited](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117118475271319244) as
evidence of non-citizens voting in the 2020 presidential election was drafted
by individuals affiliated with the Trump-aligned think tank, America First
Policy Institute.

The Center for Election Innovation & Research's David Becker told NPR the
seven-page report was "laughable" and pointed out that "Census data cannot be
reliably matched to voter data."

#### **Thursday, Aug. 20 - DOJ Tries to Interview FBI Officials Tied to Mar-a-
Lago Search**

AP [reported](https://apnews.com/article/justice-department-trump-
maralago-b561cf695c2b8476a4320b03155c3d90) that investigators at Trump's
Justice Department have made efforts to question FBI officials tied to the
2022 search of Mar-a-Lago that led to the president's indictment the following
year for unlawfully retaining classified documents.

The move is part of an investigation based in Florida seeking to establish a
conspiracy against Trump by his perceived enemies.

#### **Friday, Aug. 21 - Ballroom Construction Can Continue For Now, Supreme
Court Says**

Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts handed another victory to the Trump
administration by [allowing](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/supreme-
court/supreme-court-trump-white-house-ballroom-rcna592899) construction on the
president's White House ballroom to continue for now by pausing a lower
court's ruling that ordered a halt to the project.

Construction on the ballroom is already about [two-thirds
complete](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/18/us/politics/trump-ballroom-
construction.html), according to one White House official, with a team of 250
people working 20 hours a day, seven days a week on the project.
